item.title: U.N. experts say U.S. may have committed war crimes with 2 Iran strikes
item.description: U.N.-commissioned rights experts say there are "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes with strikes that killed scores of Iranian civilians.

item.title: Village votes to leave U.K. in symbolic protest of plan to house asylum seekers
item.description: Residents of Piddington voted overwhelmingly to leave the United Kingdom in a symbolic referendum over plans to house asylum seekers nearby.

item.title: What happens if you pay less than the minimum on your credit card?
item.description: Paying something toward your credit card bill may seem better than doing nothing, but it comes with consequences.

item.title: Tiny English village votes overwhelmingly to leave U.K. in protest of nearby asylum seeker housing
item.description: Piddington, a tiny English village of 350 people have voted overwhelmingly —285 to 26 — to "leave" the United Kingdom in a symbolic referendum over plans to house around 1,250 male asylum seekers at a military site less than a mile away. The vote had no legal force, but drew a 92% turnout.

item.title: Trump photo shows him viewing "Kennedy Center demolished" document
item.description: In court documents filed Wednesday by Rep. Joyce Beatty, a witness said he saw a "forklift run into and hit the pillars" of the building.

item.title: Senate Democrat blocks bill to shield Americans from data center energy costs
item.description: One Senate Democrat scuttled a Republican-led effort to pass legislation aimed at shielding Americans from energy costs attributed to data centers, saying it didn't go far enough.

item.title: AI is making it easier for adversaries to target U.S. military, experts say
item.description: An Iran-linked adversary used Claude AI to try to target U.S. naval forces, Anthropic revealed in a recent report.

item.title: Body of last missing hiker found after Grand Canyon flooding
item.description: Human remains found in the Grand Canyon this week have been identified as Timothy Allen Smith, the last person missing after deadly flash flooding in late August.

item.title: What the Fed's rate hike reveals about Warsh, Trump and inflation
item.description: The Fed's first rate hike in more than three years underscores the challenge of taming inflation as the Iran war drags on.

item.title: How an interest rate hike impacts farmers, middle America
item.description: The Federal Reserve spiked interest rates by 0.25 percentage points on Wednesday, sparking further concerns over the economy, especially for U.S. farmers. CBS News' Lana Zak has more.

item.title: AI makes it "easier than ever" for adversaries to target U.S. military, experts say
item.description: An Iran-linked adversary used Claude AI to try to identify U.S. naval positions and work out targeting recommendations, according to a report released by Anthropic last week. CBS News digital reporter Lauren Fichten has more.

item.title: "Godfather of AI" Geoffrey Hinton warns "we need to slow down"
item.description: King Charles is hosting a meeting for AI leaders this week amid growing concerns about the technology's oversight. Meanwhile, the "godfather of AI," Geoffrey Hinton, warned Congress this week that the industry needs to slow down development. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry reports and Brendan Bordleon, tech reporter for Politico, joins with analysis.

item.title: 1 in 3 Americans with health insurance have medical debt, survey finds
item.description: Nearly half of Americans with medical debt owe at least $2,000, forcing them to make tough choices, new research shows.

item.title: White House withdraws ICE director nominee Richard Schroyer
item.description: Richard Schroyer's nomination was held up in the Senate. The White House eventually pulled it.

item.title: 2 adults and child found dead after flooding inundates New Mexico
item.description: Navajo Nation President Buu Nygren thanked first responders for working through the night in difficult and dangerous conditions as they searched for the people.

item.title: Iran downed at least 2 American drones in recent days, U.S. officials say
item.description: Iranian forces in recent days have brought down at least two American MQ-1 unmanned aircraft, according to U.S. officials familiar with the matter.

item.title: Former U.S. Sen. Jon Kyl of Arizona dies at 84
item.description: Former U.S. Sen. Jon Kyl, who represented Arizona in both chambers of Congress over nearly three decades, has died at 84.

item.title: Canada, EU look to forge an "Alliance for the Future" amid Trump threats
item.description: Canada's leader draws regular scorn from President Trump, but European leaders gave him a standing ovation as they aim to push their ties to "the highest level."

item.title: Grand Teton park forced to kill bear due to visitors' "poor decisions"
item.description: A black bear was euthanized in Grand Teton National Park after "poor decisions" made by human visitors, according to park officials.

item.title: This Sunday: Patrick Clancy's wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, to appear on 60 Minutes
item.description: Ross Douthat sat down with Patrick Clancy and Dr. Rachel Danis just weeks after Lindsay Clancy's murder trial ended without a verdict.

item.title: GOP congresswoman says Trump immigration enforcement has "gone too far"
item.description: "The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed," said Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar.

item.title: Macklemore and Robert Kraft release dueling statements on humanitarian aid donations
item.description: Macklemore called for Robert Kraft to match his $1 million donation to Palestinian humanitarian aid relief organizations, while Kraft said he already matched a donation made by Ed Sheeran. The dueling statements came after Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran's tour for making pro-Palestinian comments onstage. Meg Oliver reports.

item.title: The current state of AI regulations as Trump pushes back on safety concerns
item.description: Calls have reached a fever pitch recently for government action on AI. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent, Ed O'Keefe and Patrick McGee have more.

item.title: Grand Canyon flood deaths lead to questions about alert system
item.description: Dr. John Giusti and Brent Rosenkranz died in major flash floods in the Grand Canyon. A third man, Timothy Allen Smith, is still missing.

item.title: 2 dead, at least 1 missing after Grand Canyon hit by flash floods
item.description: Violent flash floods hit the Grand Canyon's Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area, causing "extensive damage" to the park's water infrastructure.

item.title: 3 friends went hiking in the Grand Canyon. 2 died, 1 is still missing.
item.description: At least two people were killed after flash floods swept through parts of Grand Canyon National Park over the weekend.

item.title: Oliver Gilbert wins Democratic primary for Florida's District 24
item.description: The heavily Democratic district includes predominantly Black and Hispanic communities in northern Miami-Dade and southern Broward counties.

item.title: Estrogen, Testosterone and Menopause, Oh My!
item.description: This week on Healthful, urologist and sexual medicine specialist Dr. Rachel Rubin discusses how female bodies change during perimenopause and menopause — and explains why women may be suffering unnecessarily. Dr. Rubin and Norah discuss how vaginal hormones could save Medicare between $6 and $22 billion a year and even prevent urinary tract infections. Plus, Norah reveals her experience with menopause and hormone replacement therapy.

item.title: Border Patrol officer indicted for sexually assaulting, robbing 4 women
item.description: A Chicago Border Patrol agent is facing federal charges for allegedly sexually assaulting four women at Chicago area hotels while on the job in 2022.

item.title: 2 killed in massive warehouse explosion in Houston
item.description: The explosion at Watson Grinding and Manufacturing was felt across the city around 4:30 a.m. local time.
